title: History's Plot Twists
blurb: Empires, explorers and inventors did weirder stuff than any movie. One per card is cap.

cards.say: [a monk from Beijing met the kings of France and England in the 1280s], [Marco Polo brought pasta to Italy for the first time in 1295], [Ibn Battuta traveled about 75,000 miles in the 1300s], and [Zheng He's Chinese fleet reached East Africa in the 1410s].
cards.real: Italy had pasta before Marco Polo got home in 1295: a Genoa soldier's belongings listed a basket of macaroni back in 1279.

cards.say: [Thomas Edison's very first patent was for an electric vote counter], [a dentist helped invent the cotton candy machine], [the Super Soaker was invented by an engineer who worked on NASA missions], and [Benjamin Franklin got rich from the patents on his inventions].
cards.real: Franklin never patented any of his inventions. He wrote that since we all gain from other people's inventions, we should share ours freely.

cards.say: [Julius Caesar was the very first Roman emperor], [Roman sea walls got stronger from soaking in seawater for centuries], [ancient Greeks built a gear-driven machine that predicted eclipses], and [the Romans had a goddess who looked after the sewers].
cards.real: Caesar ruled Rome as dictator but was never emperor. His adopted heir Augustus became Rome's first emperor in 27 BC.

cards.say: [the Inca built more than 10,000 miles of roads without using the wheel], [Mansa Musa of Mali brought thousands of people on his 1324 trip to Mecca], [the Mongol Empire conquered Japan in the 1280s], and [the Ottoman Empire lasted more than 600 years].
cards.real: The Mongols tried to invade Japan in 1274 and again in 1281. Both attacks failed, and in 1281 a huge typhoon sank much of their fleet.

cards.say: [Yuri Gagarin circled Earth 17 times on the first human spaceflight], [the Apollo 11 crew filled out a customs form after coming home], [astronaut Alan Shepard hit golf balls on the Moon], and [Buzz Aldrin snapped a selfie during a spacewalk in 1966].
cards.real: Gagarin went around Earth just once, in about 108 minutes, in April 1961. Cosmonaut Gherman Titov made 17 orbits later that year.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Gagarin's Vostok 1 made a single orbit of Earth in about 108 minutes on April 12, 1961; Titov's Vostok 2 made 17 orbits in August 1961

cards.say: [the stolen 1966 World Cup trophy was found by a dog named Pickles], [a pair of Dorothy's ruby slippers was stolen in 2005 and found in 2008], [the Statue of Liberty worked as a lighthouse for 16 years], and [a real moth got stuck inside a Harvard computer in 1947].
cards.real: The ruby slippers stolen from Minnesota's Judy Garland Museum in 2005 stayed missing for 13 years, until the FBI recovered them in 2018.

cards.say: [President Gerald Ford turned down offers to play in the NFL], [Dr. Seuss wrote Green Eggs and Ham using just 50 different words], [Queen Elizabeth II trained as a mechanic during World War II], and [Napoleon's soldiers shot the nose off Egypt's Great Sphinx].
cards.real: The nose was already missing in drawings made in 1737, decades before Napoleon was born. His army didn't reach Egypt until 1798.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Dr. Seuss wrote Green Eggs and Ham (1960) with exactly 50 different words, on a bet with his publisher Bennett Cerf

cards.say: [bubble wrap was first invented to be a textured wallpaper], [the Slinky was invented by a naval engineer working with springs], [Teflon was found by accident in research on refrigerator gases], and [Velcro was inspired by the sticky feet of geckos].
cards.real: Velcro was inspired by burrs that stuck to an engineer's dog after a walk in the Swiss countryside in 1941.

cards.say: [the Eiffel Tower escaped being torn down because it was useful for radio], [the Leaning Tower of Pisa started leaning before it was finished], [King Tut's tomb was the first royal tomb found in the Valley of the Kings], and [Machu Picchu was built for an Inca emperor in the 1400s].
cards.real: Royal tombs had been found there long before, like Seti I's in 1817. Tut's, found in 1922, was special because it was still packed with treasure.

cards.say: [winners at the first modern Olympics in 1896 got gold medals], [tug-of-war was an Olympic sport until 1920], [painters and sculptors won Olympic medals until 1948], and [volleyball was invented in 1895 and first called mintonette].
cards.real: In 1896, winners got a silver medal and an olive branch. Gold medals for first place started in 1904.

cards.say: [Lewis and Clark brought a Newfoundland dog named Seaman on their trip], [Columbus sailed home from his first voyage aboard the Santa Maria], [America was named after explorer Amerigo Vespucci on a 1507 map], and [Magellan's crew left Spain with five ships and came back with one].
cards.real: The Santa Maria ran aground off Hispaniola on Christmas Day 1492, so Columbus sailed home on the smaller Niña instead.

cards.say: [the first known photo of a person shows a man getting his boots shined], [the first traffic light, put up in London in 1868, ran on gas], [Alexander Graham Bell's first phone call was to his mother], and [the first person caught speeding in a car was going 8 miles per hour].
cards.real: Bell's first call, in 1876, was to his assistant Thomas Watson in the next room, asking him to come over.
